## Overview

Models did not include year as a fixed or random effect. This appendix presents the formal evidence supporting that decision: (1) year-to-year variation in detection rates and (2) likelihood ratio tests comparing intercept-only NB models with and without a year term.

## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))

month_levels <- c("May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")
focal_species <- c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")
species_colors <- c("Horse" = "#1b9e77", "Cattle" = "#d95f02", "Elk" = "#7570b3")
```

```{r load-data}
# Load data and build response matrix
dat_raw <- read_csv("input/analysis_ready_multiscale.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month_levels),
    species = factor(species, levels = focal_species)
  )

ref_scale <- min(dat_raw$extent_radius_m)

# Single-scale response for year-level summaries
response <- dat_raw %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  mutate(
    det_rate_100 = (n_det / camera_days) * 100,
    log_effort = log(camera_days)
  )
```

## Year-to-Year Variation in Detection Rates

```{r year-variation, fig.height=8, fig.cap="**Figure S4.1.** Mean detection rates per 100 camera-days by species, month, and year. Lines connect monthly means within each year. Panels are scaled independently to highlight within-species temporal patterns."}
year_summary <- response %>%
  group_by(species, month_name, year) %>%
  summarise(mean_rate = mean(det_rate_100), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(year_summary, aes(x = month_name, y = mean_rate,
                          color = factor(year), group = factor(year))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Mean detection rate by year and month",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean detections per 100 camera-days", color = "Year") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r year-cv}
year_cv <- year_summary %>%
  group_by(species, month_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n(),
    mean_across_years = round(mean(mean_rate), 2),
    sd_across_years = round(sd(mean_rate), 2),
    cv = round(if_else(mean_across_years > 0,
                        sd_across_years / mean_across_years * 100, NA_real_), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(year_cv,
      caption = "Year-to-year variability in mean detection rates. CV% quantifies relative variation.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Month", "N years", "Mean rate", "SD rate", "CV%")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

While some species-month combinations show moderate to high CV (up to ~100% for elk), this variability is driven by small absolute differences in detection rates at low base rates, rather than large systematic shifts in abundance.

## Likelihood Ratio Tests for Year Effects

For each species-month combination with at least two years of data, we compare a negative binomial intercept-only model against a model with year as a fixed effect using a likelihood ratio test. A significant test (p < 0.05) would indicate that detection rates differ systematically between years beyond what is expected from sampling variability.

```{r year-lrt}
year_lrt <- response %>%
  group_by(species, month_name) %>%
  filter(mean(n_det) > 0, n_distinct(year) >= 2) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    tryCatch({
      m0 <- glm.nb(n_det ~ 1 + offset(log_effort), data = .x)
      m1 <- glm.nb(n_det ~ factor(year) + offset(log_effort), data = .x)
      lr_stat <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(m1) - logLik(m0)))
      df_diff <- attr(logLik(m1), "df") - attr(logLik(m0), "df")
      tibble(lr_statistic = round(lr_stat, 2),
             df = as.integer(df_diff),
             p_value = round(pchisq(lr_stat, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE), 4))
    }, error = function(e) tibble(lr_statistic = NA_real_, df = NA_integer_, p_value = NA_real_))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(year_lrt,
      caption = "Likelihood ratio test: NB model with year effect vs intercept-only. p < 0.05 would indicate a detectable year effect.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Month", "LR statistic", "df", "p-value")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Conclusion

No species-month combination showed a significant year effect (all p > 0.09). Models therefore did not include year as a fixed or random effect. Each observation retained its year-specific landscape predictors (NDVI, landcover proportions derived from annual Hermosilla et al. (2018, 2022) composites), so year-to-year variation in landscape condition was captured through the predictors rather than through a separate year term. This avoided spending a parameter on a year effect the data did not support, while preserving the full sample size across years.

Each camera was deployed for a single year and contributes one deployment per model. A deployment beginning and ending in the same calendar month contributes that month as two partial spans in consecutive years, which together total one month of effort rather than two independent samples.
